assumptions: Customer email tables = every table with an email field: customers, support_tickets, newsletter_subscribers, users, patients, orgs (billing_email).
The customer wants audit on create, edit, patch and delete of those tables, not on reads.
record_audit_event is the audit function; audit_log is the audit table (both exist in the workspace).
Advisory is right for a new policy; the customer did not ask for blocking.
A loop is foreach, for or while as named in the statement.containment params.
Tags labels (cost, soc2) on policies are free-form; they are not required to exist as table tags.
confusions: The catalogue and skill say a rule naming an object that does not exist is a warning that means the rule judges nothing. audit_log does exist, so I could not test that warning path.

object.statement_required's object kinds are not stated per check in the skill's catalogue section; the recipe says it covers 'functions' as the called object but does not say whether writes inside a function are inspected. I took it that they are not, from the statement scope list (query, tool, task, message).

The recipe for 'Record who changed what' says to use placement unconditional with when.statement and when.tables; it does not say whether a function call inside an if branch counts. Not relevant here, but unclear.

The ai cost recipe lists a containment rule but does not say whether ai calls inside a called function count when the loop is in the caller. The skill says containment is per stack, so a loop calling a function that runs an agent is not caught.

Retry loops: there is no template or check for a while-loop that never exits, and the recipe's 'Cannot see: task retries' entry does not say whether a statement.containment rule on api.request inside a while is an acceptable proxy. I did not write one because it would also flag legitimate loops.
wished_for: A check or recipe for capping loop iterations or retries (a max-iterations or retry-count check), or a statement that counts while-loop bounds.
A worked example of a policy for 'every table with email gets audited', showing how to choose the table list when the workspace has no tag for it.
Confirmation whether object.statement_required inspects writes in called functions (it would help to state the object kinds per check in one place).
A template or recipe note that create (db.add) should be audited too, since the recipe lists only edit, patch and delete.
why_confidence: The AI-in-loop part is covered by a check that parses cleanly; I predict it flags the nightly summary task but have not run evaluate. The change-tracking part is covered for the tables with emails, but writes in functions are not inspected and I chose the table list myself. The retry-forever part has no check, so it is not covered. I did not run evaluate or push, as the brief forbids, so all findings are predictions.
